answer: Arrival-Skew Quota Gating. Each identity gets a fixed registration allowance per time slice, and the slice boundary is offset by a per-identity pigment drawn from its declared origin, so a batch of clones all land in the same narrow window and exhaust one shared quota. A lone grove of honest identities spreads naturally across slices and never contends. To fake spread, an attacker must hold each clone back until its own offset, forcing one voyage of traffic per identity across many slices and paying real queueing delay plus lost throughput on every one.
